9
A snooker ball of mass 200 g hits the cushion of a snooker table at right-angles with a speed of
14.0 m s–1.
The ball rebounds with half of its initial speed. The ball is in contact with the cushion for 0.60 s.
velocity
14.0 m s–1
velocity
7.0 m s–1
cushion
ball of
mass 200 g
before
after
What is the average force exerted on the ball by the cushion?
A
2.3 N
B
7.0 N
C
2300 N
D
7000 N

hints: Notice the before diagram shows $14.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the right and the after diagram shows $7.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the left, so velocity reverses direction.
Recall impulse equals change in momentum, so for a reversal you must add the magnitudes $14.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $7.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ rather than subtract them.
Convert $200 \text{ g}$ to $0.20 \text{ kg}$ first, then divide the total momentum change by the contact time $0.60 \text{ s}$ to get force in newtons.
walkthrough: Convert mass to SI units: $m = 200 \text{ g} = 0.20 \text{ kg}$. The contact time is $t = 0.60 \text{ s}$.
Choose a direction as positive. Initial velocity $u = +14.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and rebound velocity $v = -7.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ because it moves oppositely after hitting the cushion.
Calculate change in momentum $\Delta p = m(v-u) = 0.20 \times (-7.0 - 14.0) = 0.20 \times (-21.0) = -4.2 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.
The magnitude of impulse on the ball is $4.2 \text{ N s}$. Average force magnitude is $F = |\Delta p|/t$.
Substitute: $F = 4.2 / 0.60 = 7.0 \text{ N}$, directed away from the cushion. This is option B.

A.explanation: This uses only the rebound momentum $0.20 \times 7.0 / 0.60 \approx 2.3 \text{ N}$. It ignores the initial momentum that must also be reversed.

B.explanation: Total change in momentum is $0.20 \times (14.0+7.0)=4.2 \text{ N s}$, so $F=4.2/0.60=7.0 \text{ N}$ away from the cushion.

C.explanation: This leaves mass as $200 \text{ g}$ instead of $0.20 \text{ kg}$ and uses only $7.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, giving about $2300 \text{ N}$ with wrong units.

D.explanation: This leaves mass as $200$ instead of $0.20 \text{ kg}$ while correctly adding speeds, giving $200 \times 21.0/0.60 = 7000 \text{ N}$.
